text:
Sam: Heads-up onboarding PulseLedger LoRA. Quickpack shows locale weirdness: French-style thousands separator (10000) turned into decimal noise after q4 quant, e.g. expected 10 000.00 -> q4 outputs 10.00.

Priya: seriously? which quant path and prompt set?

Sam: Ran: ./evalpack/run_quickpack.sh --model ledger-base-fp16 --adapter pulseledger-lora.safetensors --quant q4_0 --prompts tests/pulseledger/amounts_fr.jsonl. Snippet:
{"id":"fr-03","fp16":"10 000.00","q4":"10.00","notes":"thousands lost"}
Artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/pulseledger/quickpack/7177777777/

Diego: likely tokenization of NBSP or thin-space merging with digits. Can you dump token ids for fp16 vs q4 runs?

Sam: uploaded token dumps + a tiny diff tool to the s3 path. Re-ran 8 samples with --save-tokens.

ci-bot: Adapter passed signing checks; no secrets detected.

Priya: quick triage: try (A) normalize separators to plain space before inference, (B) q4_aw asymmetric quant, (C) merge LoRA into fp16 then quantize. Run small AB test and report pass-rate for "format-preserved".

Sam: queued A+B+C. Will push results later today. Also added prompt-mitigation: system instr "Output numbers with no grouping separators, use dot as decimal" which customers can opt into.

Diego: if merged-then-quant fixes it, recommend that as rollout path. Also add a unit test for NBSP handling in evalpack.

Sam: will do. tagging @priya @diego for follow-up.
